name: syncope overview
title: Syncope decision chart: confirm a transient loss of consciousness, then the history's red flags split benign reflex (vasovagal) syncope from cardiac syncope, which is obstructive, bradycardic or tachycardic; each column gives the clues, the investigations in order and the treatment

root.title: A faint: was it SYNCOPE, and are there RED FLAGS for a CARDIAC cause?
lines: syncope = transient loss of consciousness from low brain blood flow, recovering on its own
first CONFIRM it: not a trip, weakness or dizziness
not a mimic: seizure, stroke or transient ischemic attack, brain bleed, hypoglycemia, hypoxia, psychogenic
the HISTORY sorts it: circumstances, prodrome, recovery, witnesses, heart disease, family history of sudden death

groups.title: NO red flags: a trigger + a prodrome
lines: REFLEX syncope: the most common, benign

groups.title: RED FLAGS → CARDIAC syncope: the worst prognosis
lines: syncope DURING exertion, SUDDEN with no prodrome, known heart disease, an abnormal ECG, or a family history of sudden death or drowning

pres.title: 1 · Bloods, ECG, ECHO  →  2 · Ambulatory monitor: match symptoms to rhythm  →  3 · Provoke: tilt, stress test, electrophysiology (EP) study
lines: ~monitors only help if another episode happens while it is worn: Holter 24–48 h, external or implantable loop recorder

head: h
Vasovagal (reflex) syncope
structurally normal heart, any age
also situational, orthostatic, carotid sinus
clue: • standing long, a warm day, after a meal
inv: sinus slowing + AV block TOGETHER = vasovagal
tx: • prodrome: SIT or LIE down, cross and squeeze the legs

head: h
Obstruction
aortic stenosis, hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM), cardiac tumour, pulmonary embolism
clue: • HCM: sudden death in the young and healthy

head: h
Bradyarrhythmia
see the BRADYCARDIA chart
clue: • 'what is the last thing you remember?'
inv: • left or right bundle branch block

head: h
Tachyarrhythmia
see the TACHYCARDIA chart
clue: • prior myocardial infarction, poor ejection fraction
